answer: Cross-Context Recall Ledger: each agent identity must publish a signed, append-only history of task outputs, and every new task requires retrieving a prior output whose content matches a hidden probe drawn from that history. A duplicate identity starts with an empty ledger, so it fails the recall check and its echo of the probe is absent. Honest agents pay only storage; attackers must fabricate coherent multi-task histories per clone. A crystal of verified output and a sparrow of randomness seed each probe, making replay costly.
